misconceptions.description: Writing an Ethobot debrief that reports that students enjoyed the activity rather than marking where ethical reasoning actually moved
misconceptions.trigger: debrief note describes mood or participation but no shift in argument
misconceptions.feedback: Mark where the reasoning changed, not whether students had fun. Find the turn that moved the argument.

misconceptions.description: Evaluating an ethical dilemma (such as facial recognition for attendance) only on whether it works, ignoring who bears the error cost or rights at stake
misconceptions.trigger: student or annotation frames the decision purely as effectiveness
misconceptions.feedback: Add the rights-and-error frame. Ask who is most likely to be wrongly affected, not only whether the tool works.

misconceptions.description: Annotating that reasoning improved without pinning the change to a specific transcript turn or the prompt that caused it
misconceptions.trigger: debrief claims growth but cites no turn number or triggering question
misconceptions.feedback: Locate the pivot. Name the turn where the reasoning changed and the question that caused it.

misconceptions.description: Accepting Ethobot's framing as the correct ethical answer instead of treating it as a prompt for student judgment
misconceptions.trigger: student adopts the bot's position without weighing it
misconceptions.feedback: Ethobot raises questions, it does not settle them. Judge its prompts against the rights and costs in the case.
